reaper man.title: Reaper Man
reaper man.author: Terry Pratchett
reaper man.why: Discworld novel where Death takes a holiday to live as a farmhand; funny, warm and surprisingly moving about mortality.

water knife.title: The Water Knife
water knife.author: Paolo Bacigalupi
water knife.why: Near-future thriller about water wars in the American Southwest, praised for feeling uncomfortably plausible.

eleanor oliphant is completely fine.title: Eleanor Oliphant is Completely Fine
eleanor oliphant is completely fine.author: Gail Honeyman
eleanor oliphant is completely fine.why: A lonely, socially awkward woman slowly opens up; readers find it funny, heartbreaking and a gradual reveal.

river is waiting.title: The River Is Waiting
river is waiting.author: Wally Lamb
river is waiting.why: A family drama about addiction and loss that readers find devastating but powerful.

coraline.title: Coraline
coraline.author: Neil Gaiman
coraline.why: A short, genuinely creepy tale of a girl and her sinister other mother, scary even for adults.

martin eden.title: Martin Eden
martin eden.author: Jack London
martin eden.why: A working-class sailor tries to become a writer; readers say it broke them and mirrors their own ambition.

eye of the bedlam bride.title: The Eye of the Bedlam Bride
eye of the bedlam bride.author: Matt Dinniman
eye of the bedlam bride.why: Latest in the Dungeon Crawler Carl LitRPG series; fans love the dark humour and relentless inventiveness.

exordia.title: Exordia
exordia.author: Seth Dickinson
exordia.why: Cutting-edge sci-fi with strange alien tech and body horror; readers call it wild, with strong prose.

woman in me.title: The Woman in Me
woman in me.author: Britney Spears
woman in me.why: The pop star tells her own story of fame and control; readers find it honest and heartbreaking.

currently reading.title: Currently Reading
currently reading.author: Teecee Design Studio
currently reading.why: Not a book; a generic phrase from reading-thread posts.

from the mixed up files of mrs basil e f.title: From the Mixed-Up Files of Mrs. Basil E. Frankweiler
from the mixed up files of mrs basil e f.author: E. L. Konigsburg
from the mixed up files of mrs basil e f.why: Two siblings run away to live in a New York museum and chase a mystery; a beloved children's classic.

fellowship of the ring.title: The Fellowship of the Ring
fellowship of the ring.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
fellowship of the ring.why: First part of The Lord of the Rings, the foundational quest fantasy that readers return to again.

bury your gays.title: Bury Your Gays
bury your gays.author: Chuck Tingle
bury your gays.why: Mostly mixed or negative reception in the comments.

sound of gravel.title: The sound of gravel
sound of gravel.author: Ruth Wariner
sound of gravel.why: A woman's account of growing up in a polygamist Mormon family in Mexico; tragic and gripping.

sophies world.title: Sophie's World
sophies world.author: Jostein Gaarder
sophies world.why: A teenager gets letters teaching her the history of philosophy inside a mystery; an accessible entry to the subject.

elantris.title: Elantris
elantris.author: Brandon Sanderson
elantris.why: Sanderson's debut about a fallen magical city and the people trapped in it; fans praise its imagery and plot.

making of the atomic bomb.title: The making of the atomic bomb
making of the atomic bomb.author: Richard Rhodes
making of the atomic bomb.why: Comprehensive, award-winning history of how the bomb was built, from the physics to the people; readers find it gripping.

reincarnation blues.title: Reincarnation blues
reincarnation blues.author: Michael Poore
reincarnation blues.why: A soul reincarnated thousands of times tries to get life right while loving Death; funny and warm.

flashlight.title: Flashlight
flashlight.author: Susan Choi
flashlight.why: Comments are split, with an abandoned read and lukewarm reactions.

hidden valley road.title: Hidden Valley Road
hidden valley road.author: Robert Kolker
hidden valley road.why: True story of a family with many schizophrenic sons, reading like a novel and tracing the history of the illness.

adventures of huckleberry finn.title: The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
adventures of huckleberry finn.author: Mark Twain
adventures of huckleberry finn.why: A boy and a runaway slave drift down the Mississippi in Twain's satire of American society.

trilogy.title: Trilogy
trilogy.author: Jon Fosse
trilogy.why: Comments do not discuss this book; wrong match.

forge of god.title: The forge of God
forge of god.author: Greg Bear
forge of god.why: Hard sci-fi about Earth's destruction by alien machines, called stunning by readers who rate it among the best apocalypse novels.

killing star.title: The killing star
killing star.author: Charles R. Pellegrino and George Zebrowski
killing star.why: Hard sci-fi about a ruthless alien first strike, loved for its cold logic on first contact.

invisible women.title: Invisible Women
invisible women.author: Caroline Criado Perez
invisible women.why: Shows with data how a world designed around men harms women; readers find it eye-opening and infuriating.

tau zero.title: Tau Zero
tau zero.author: Poul Anderson
tau zero.why: A starship that can't stop accelerating hurtles through cosmic time; a classic of hard sci-fi, though some find it heavy on physics.

lords of discipline.title: The Lords of Discipline
lords of discipline.author: Pat Conroy
lords of discipline.why: A cadet at a Southern military academy confronts a secret society; praised for lyrical prose and powerful storytelling.

maid.title: The Maid
maid.author: Nita Prose
maid.why: Mixed to negative reception in the comments.

arrival.title: Stories of Your Life and Others
arrival.author: Ted Chiang
arrival.why: Ted Chiang's thoughtful, precise short stories, including the one behind the film Arrival, widely named among the best sf collections.

plot.title: The Plot
plot.author: Jean Hanff Korelitz
plot.why: A writer learns someone is stealing a plot he took from a student; readers enjoy the twisty literary thriller.

stainless steel rat.title: The Stainless Steel Rat
stainless steel rat.author: Harry Harrison
stainless steel rat.why: A roguish space con man is recruited to catch other criminals; a light, fun classic though some find it dated.

iron widow.title: Iron Widow
iron widow.author: Xiran Jay Zhao
iron widow.why: A mecha reimagining of China's only empress, with a furious heroine; readers call it a fun sci-fi and fantasy blend.

under the volcano.title: Under the Volcano
under the volcano.author: Malcolm Lowry
under the volcano.why: A British consul drinks himself toward ruin on the Day of the Dead in Mexico; lush, demanding modernist prose.

greenlights.title: Greenlights
greenlights.author: Matthew McConaughey
greenlights.why: The actor's stories and life lessons in a distinctive voice; readers like it, especially as an audiobook.

never flinch.title: Never Flinch
never flinch.author: Stephen King
never flinch.why: Comments mostly critical of the ending and quality.

hollow places.title: The Hollow Places
hollow places.author: T. Kingfisher
hollow places.why: A woman finds a portal to a strange otherworld through a museum wall; creepy with dark humour.

young mungo.title: Young Mungo
young mungo.author: Douglas Stuart
young mungo.why: A teenager in Glasgow falls for a boy from the rival religion; devastating and long remembered by readers.

mysterious benedict society.title: The Mysterious Benedict Society
mysterious benedict society.author: Trenton Lee Stewart
mysterious benedict society.why: Gifted children go undercover at a strange school to stop a villain; a clever adventure good for read-aloud.

kings of the wyld.title: Kings of the wyld
kings of the wyld.author: Nicholas Eames
kings of the wyld.why: A band of ageing mercenaries reunite for one last mission; fans compare it to a fun D&D campaign.

bag of bones.title: Bag of Bones
bag of bones.author: Stephen King
bag of bones.why: A widowed novelist is haunted at his lakeside house; a slow, emotional ghost story some call King's favourite.

road to tender hearts.title: The Road to Tender Hearts
road to tender hearts.author: Annie Hartnett
road to tender hearts.why: A quirky road trip story described as funny, sentimental and addictive, with a Wes Anderson feel.

last question.title: The Last Question
last question.author: Isaac Asimov
last question.why: A brief Asimov story tracing humanity's question about entropy across eons; named a favourite short story by many.

jade city.title: Jade City
jade city.author: Fonda Lee
jade city.why: Mafia-style clans fight over magical jade in an Asian-inspired city; a sweeping, rich family saga.

harsh mistress.title: The moon is a harsh mistress
harsh mistress.author: Robert A. Heinlein
harsh mistress.why: A lunar colony rebels against Earth with the help of a self-aware computer; a classic, though not all like it.

strength of the few.title: The Strength of the Few
strength of the few.author: James Islington
strength of the few.why: Sequel to The Will of the Many in a Roman-style magical world; fans find it gripping though some find the series overhyped.

hearing trumpet.title: The hearing trumpet
hearing trumpet.author: Leonora Carrington
hearing trumpet.why: An old woman with an ear trumpet stumbles into cults and apocalypse in a surreal, absurd romp.

quiet.title: Quiet
quiet.author: Susan Cain
quiet.why: Explains the strengths of introverts; readers say it helped them accept themselves.

columbine.title: Columbine
columbine.author: Dave Cullen
columbine.why: A careful, vivid account of the school shooting and its investigation; hard material but compulsively readable.

children.title: The Children
children.author: Melissa Albert
children.why: Comments discuss other books; wrong match.

crimson petal and the white.title: The Crimson Petal and the White
crimson petal and the white.author: Michel Faber
crimson petal and the white.why: A prostitute climbs through Victorian London in a lush, immersive novel; readers praise it but find it bleak.

virgin suicides.title: The Virgin Suicides
virgin suicides.author: Jeffrey Eugenides
virgin suicides.why: Neighbourhood boys try to understand five sisters in 1970s suburbia; haunting and lyrical.

lost city of z.title: The Lost City of Z
lost city of z.author: David Grann
lost city of z.why: A journalist follows explorer Percy Fawcett's vanished search for a lost Amazon city; gripping adventure non-fiction.

portrait of a lady.title: The Portrait of a Lady
portrait of a lady.author: Henry James
portrait of a lady.why: A spirited American heiress's choices in Europe unfold in James's subtle prose; some find it improves as it goes.

space opera.title: Space Opera
space opera.author: Catherynne M. Valente
space opera.why: Earth must do well in a galactic song contest to survive; a flamboyant, absurd Eurovision-style romp.

system of the world.title: System of the World
system of the world.author: Neal Stephenson
system of the world.why: Closing volume of Stephenson's Baroque Cycle, a vast historical saga of science, money and intrigue in Newton's England.

ship of fools.title: Ship of fools
ship of fools.author: Richard Paul Russo
ship of fools.why: A grim space-horror tale aboard a starship encountering something terrible; a favourite of readers who like dark sf.

rabbit run.title: Rabbit, Run
rabbit run.author: John Updike
rabbit run.why: A restless former basketball star abandons his family; praised for prose style though the main character is unlikable.

skinny legs and all.title: Skinny Legs and All
skinny legs and all.author: Tom Robbins
skinny legs and all.why: Tom Robbins' playful, eccentric novel about art, religion and a giant turkey-shaped camper.

good person.title: A Good Person
good person.author: Kirsten King
good person.why: Readers enjoy spending time in the head of a deranged, difficult narrator in this darkly comic novel.

manhunt.title: Manhunt
manhunt.author: Gretchen Felker-Martin
manhunt.why: A queer, brutal post-apocalyptic horror novel readers describe as dark and unflinching.

witches.title: The Witches
witches.author: Roald Dahl
witches.why: Dahl's classic about a boy facing child-hating witches; so gripping it turned some kids into readers.

juice.title: Juice
juice.author: Tim Winton
juice.why: Winton's bleak post-collapse Australian journey, compared to The Road in a Mad Max setting.

little princess.title: A Little Princess
little princess.author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
little princess.why: A girl's fortunes collapse at boarding school but her imagination keeps her going; a gentle children's classic.

less than zero.title: Less than Zero
less than zero.author: Bret Easton Ellis
less than zero.why: Bret Easton Ellis' debut of bored, drugged Los Angeles youth; disturbing and cold, a cult favourite.

victorian psycho.title: Victorian Psycho
victorian psycho.author: Virginia Feito
victorian psycho.why: A governess in a Victorian household turns violent; readers call it unhinged, funny and gothic.

lucky jim.title: Lucky Jim
lucky jim.author: Kingsley Amis
lucky jim.why: A hapless junior lecturer stumbles through academic life; praised as one of the funniest novels ever.

five little indians.title: Five Little Indians
five little indians.author: Michelle Good
five little indians.why: Five residential-school survivors try to rebuild their lives; readers find it heartbreaking and powerful.

me before you.title: Me Before You
me before you.author: Jojo Moyes
me before you.why: A carer and a paralysed man fall in love; readers say it made them cry, though its themes are debated.

tell the wolves im home.title: Tell the Wolves I'm Home
tell the wolves im home.author: Carol Rifka Brunt
tell the wolves im home.why: A teenager grieves her uncle lost to AIDS in the 1980s and forms an unexpected friendship; tender and moving.

lion women of tehran.title: The Lion Women of Tehran
lion women of tehran.author: Marjan Kamali
lion women of tehran.why: Two Iranian women's friendship across decades of upheaval; readers name it a top favourite.
